steps.what: Read the supply card before this round.
Select classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.
Store classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.
Order classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.
Issue classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.
Inventory classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.

tasks.design: A year colleague writes a supply card before the round. The card holds the item name, the cupboard, and the last count title. The teacher reads the card, then still selects, stores, orders on paper or by phone, issues, and counts the materials. If the card has no row, the teacher reads the paper cupboard list inside the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The cupboard row sat in a folder the teacher opened at the start of the round.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper supply card with the item name, the cupboard, and the last count title is enough to start. No system is required.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing, storing, ordering, issuing, and counting the materials still take the time.
tasks.human_edge: Only the teacher can judge which materials this class needs.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the cupboard row. The teacher still selects, stores, orders, issues, and counts.

reach.task: Count one cupboard of classroom materials
reach.learn: The card names the cupboard. The technician still writes the count.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the item name, the cupboard, and the last count title shortens the search when the row is there. The teacher still selects, stores, orders, issues, and counts. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The workplace is a mid-size European secondary school.
A year colleague writes the supply card before the round.
Fields are the item name, the cupboard, and the last count title.
The teacher selects, stores, orders on paper or by phone, issues, and counts at full time.
The paper order is the teacher's own note. It is not posted anywhere else.
The supply card does not hold the new count or the items chosen.
If the row is missing, the teacher reads the paper cupboard list inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because a year colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Staff and parent consent for a monitoring or scoring tool is out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether this school already keeps a one-line supply card for each cupboard.
research_questions: How often a first round has no row on the supply card.

incremental.description: No extra teacher upkeep. A year colleague keeps the supply card.
A year colleague writes the supply card: item name, cupboard, and last count title.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The round is the first one, so the supply card has no row and the teacher reads the paper cupboard list. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tutor a pupil and consult the school.

steps.what: Read the visit card before this trip.
Visit schools to tutor students with sensory impairments.
Consult with teachers regarding students' special needs.
outputs: what the school teacher was told

tasks.design: A year colleague writes a visit card before the trip. The card holds the school name, the pupil name, and the teacher name. The teacher reads the card, then still visits the school, tutors the pupil, and consults the teachers. If the card has no row, the teacher reads the paper school list inside the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The school row sat in a folder the teacher opened before the trip.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper visit card with the school name, the pupil name, and the teacher name is enough to start. No system is required.
tasks.still_hard: Tutoring the pupil and consulting the teachers still take the time.
tasks.human_edge: Only the teacher can judge how to tutor this pupil and what to tell the school.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the school row. The teacher still tutors the pupil and consults the teachers.

reach.task: Tutor one pupil on a school visit
reach.learn: The card names the school. The teacher still tutors the pupil.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the school name, the pupil name, and the teacher name shortens the search when the row is there. The teacher still tutors and consults. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The workplace is a mid-size European secondary school.
A year colleague writes the visit card before the trip.
Fields are the school name, the pupil name, and the teacher name.
The teacher visits, tutors, and consults at full time.
The visit card does not hold the pupil's needs.
If the row is missing, the teacher reads the paper school list inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because a year colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Staff and parent consent for a monitoring or scoring tool is out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether this school already keeps a one-line visit card for each trip.
research_questions: How often a first trip has no row on the visit card.

incremental.description: No extra teacher upkeep. A year colleague keeps the visit card.
A year colleague writes the visit card: school name, pupil name, and teacher name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The trip is the first one, so the visit card has no row and the teacher reads the paper school list. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher still selects, stores, orders, issues, and counts classroom materials, and still visits schools to tutor and consult. A card only shortens finding the cupboard or the school.
reach: Library Technicians: count one cupboard after the card names it.
Special Education Teachers, Elementary School: tutor one pupil on a school visit the card has named.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper list when the card has no row.
Decide from the cupboard and the pupil, not from the card.
role.ambitious_version: Cards do not select, order, count, tutor, or consult. The special education teacher still does.
